messages:
maria: Heads-up — since ~09:04 UTC we're seeing intermittent packet loss inside the us-east-2 GPU clusters. Symptoms are application-level retransmits and occasional gRPC hangs between pods on different nodes.

lee: Is this limited to a particular node pool or AZ?

maria: Looks concentrated to gpu-pool-2 in az-a and az-b, but not 100% reproducible. Kernel counters show TX drops on some nodes right when requests spike.

devon: Any pattern with autoscale events? GPU churn?

maria: Yep, correlates with scheduled autoscale-in/out events (pods and nodes). Noticed loss window ~30s after node join/leave. Also spikier when model-serving pps jumps.

anita: Which overlay are we using on these nodes? Geneve or VXLAN?

maria: Geneve. ethtool and ip link show offloads differ across NICs. Sending a dump from node gpu-a-12:

```
$ ip link show geneve0
3: geneve0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1450 qdisc pfifo_fast state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
$ ethtool -k eth0 | grep -i tso
tcp-segmentation-offload: on
generic-segmentation-offload: on
```

maria: Note MTU set to 1450 (we use lower MTU for encapsulation). But one node showed mtu 1500 on the host within a few minutes which coincided with drops.

samir: Could be a path-MTU blackhole or offload mismatch where encapsulated packets get fragmented/ dropped by NIC or switch. Any dmesg/kernel errors?

maria: Found this on gpu-b-03 dmesg around the time of loss:
```
mlx5_core 0000:5e:00.0: NIC Link changed from up to down
mlx5_core 0000:5e:00.0: firmware reset
```

lee: So mlx5 reset during autoscale? That can flush flow tables and temporarily break encapsulation state. Also RDMA-related resets sometimes flip offloads.

devon: Do we see ECN/DSCP rewriting on the fabric? Some ToR firmware upgrades changed GSO handling in the past.

anita: Quick checks to run:
- `ss -s` on nodes during spike
- `tc -s qdisc show dev eth0` for drops
- `bridge fdb show` to ensure geneve endpoints present
- check kube-proxy/node agent logs

maria: Ran tc and see qdisc drops on eth0 on affected nodes:
```
qdisc mq on dev eth0
 Sent 1.2GiB, received 900MiB
 backlog 0b requeues 0
  drop 12345
```

samir: 12k drops — pretty significant. Might be the qdisc fallback when GSO/TCP offload fails. Try toggling GSO/TSO off as a quick test on a canary node:
```
ethtool -K eth0 tso off gso off gro off
```

maria: Did that on gpu-a-12 and loss stopped for that node during the next spike. Performance hit ~5% CPU increase but no p99 tail spikes.

lee: That points at offload mismatch. Long term we need consistent offload and MTU config across the fleet and handle NIC resets during node lifecycle.

devon: Action items:
1) Roll a canary cluster with consistent ethtool config and MTU pinned to 1450 in cloud-init (gpu-pool-2-canary). (assigned: devon)
2) Add kernel/uplink reset detection in node agent to re-apply offload/mtu on NIC reorder (assigned: anita)
3) Check if autoscaler is cordoning/draining in a way that triggers NIC teardown before pod migration (assigned: lee)
4) Short-term: apply `tso/gso/gro off` via daemonset to affected pool while investigating (assigned: maria)

anita: Also schedule vendor FW check for mlx5 in az-a/az-b — firmware resets frequent.

net-bot: @channel detected repeated mlx5 firmware resets on 7 nodes in gpu-pool-2 across az-a, az-b between 09:04-09:12 UTC. Creating incident CL-2026-137.

maria: I'll roll the daemonset with offload disable to 10% of nodes first. Will post results in 10m.

samir: FYI this pattern can also manifest as asymmetric path MTU: encapsulated packet > underlay MTU -> switch drops -> no ICMP back. We might want to enable iptables/icmp logs for PMTUD in canary.

maria: Update: after disabling offloads on 2 canary nodes we saw zero application retransmits on those nodes during the next spike. Scheduling wider rollout now.

lee: Good. Let's keep monitoring and converge on firmware/driver fix rather than long-term disabling offloads.

maria: Will open a tracking PR with the diagnostic logs and a runbook for on-call. Attaching packet captures and ethtool outputs in the incident ticket.
